title: GPT-6 Astra, Looped Transformers, and Hidden Reasoning
author: Sebastian Raschka
updated_note: two small additions since the first archived copy (9 September 13:59 UTC): a link to his earlier video, and, on 2 October after a reader's comment, a sentence on OpenAI's ARC-AGI-3 harness post; the argument is unchanged. A shorter note of 2 September on his blog made the same case first
takeaway: An explainer of looped transformers written against GPT-6 Astra's reported use of them: reusing a stack of blocks saves weights but not compute or KV cache, so Raschka argues a looped model behaves like a bigger one and does not by itself hide its chain of thought. It rests on published papers and on a reading of OpenAI's system card, not on any measurement of Astra.
verdict: Believe the mechanics, which we checked against Nanbeige4.2-3B's config and the papers. Treat "looping does not hide reasoning" as half right: it does not remove the written chain, but the equivalence with a bigger model breaks when keys and values are shared across passes, and later measurements found looping raises reasoning without a chain of thought more than it raises general ability.

discussion.t: Hacker News: GPT-6 Astra, looped transformers, and hidden reasoning

responses.t: How concerned should we be about Astra's recurrent architecture?
responses.n: A week before the article: agrees a looped transformer is not an RNN and that a 32-layer model looped twice is no harder to monitor than a 64-layer one, and guesses three or four loops from Pachocki's "within a factor of two". Its worry is the dial: a loop count turned up later, when about 1.3 times the layers already doubles a model's no-CoT time horizon.

responses.t: GPT-6 Astra can do a lot of multi-hop reasoning without chain of thought
responses.n: Hours before the article: 24 made-up multi-hop questions, at least 20 samples each, zero reasoning tokens. Astra was never worse than GPT-5.6 Sol and handled about 4 to 5 hops where Sol managed 2 to 3. Informal, by its author's account, but a measurement of Astra, which the article has none of.

responses.t: Recurrent KV-cache sharing may undermine the bounded-depth argument for CoT monitorability
responses.n: The mechanism the article's cache section misses (section 8): if early passes read keys written by later passes of earlier tokens, as in the Huginn paper's cache sharing, hidden depth grows with the answer. A follow-up mental-arithmetic benchmark put Astra's 50% horizon about 4 times Sol's, with the caveat that Astra shortcuts some tasks statistically.

A reader quoted the system card's controllability numbers (93% against 48%); the author answered that needing less reasoning is efficiency, and the reader replied that the card measures length and controllability separately. Another asked about early exits and missing keys (section 3); a third pointed to OpenAI's ARC-AGI-3 harness post, which the author added on 2 October.

responses.t: GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches the no-CoT performance of GPT-6 Astra
responses.n: On 27 no-CoT tasks, GPT-6.1 Sol closes 80% (95% CI 72 to 87%) of the gap from GPT-6 Sol to Astra. His explanation, unconfirmed, is that 6.1 Sol is a smaller looped model; if so, its Astra-like controllability weakly suggests the architecture does matter for monitorability.

responses.t: Looping a transformer increases no-CoT capabilities more than general capabilities
responses.by: Alek Westover and Nick Kuhn (Alignment Forum)
responses.n: The first test of the article's question on an open looped model, NVIDIA's Dory 4B: 1 to 8 loops raised no-CoT reasoning (NCRI) by about 18 points while general ability (mini-ECI) moved at most about 1.5, worth about 2 NCRI points on the trend. In recurrent cache mode, under RL against a CoT monitor, it learned to solve tasks behind almost all-filler chains. One small model, single seeds, no matched non-looped control; Neel Nanda's comment finds most of the jump in 2 of 19 task domains.

since.n: OpenAI's successor flagship. Like the Astra announcement and system card, it says nothing about the architecture: the looped design is still known only from reporting and from OpenAI researchers' replies to it.

Jakub Pachocki's longer post. It proposes perplexity-based limits that labs would not cross until a successor to CoT monitors exists, and expects alignment auditing to keep degrading; it does not describe Astra's architecture or return to looping.

resources.t: GPT-6 Astra system card: CoT controllability and monitorability
resources.n: What the article summarises in two sentences: controllability 60.9% against 16.1% for GPT-5.6 Sol (chains of 750 to 1,250 tokens), UK AISI's 93% against 48% and no-CoT math time horizon of 30.9 minutes against 3.6, and OpenAI's view that controllability is not differentially due to architecture.
The short note the article grew from ("Let's debunk this a bit"), with Nanbeige's 75% token efficiency, which the article leaves out.

resources.t: Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Model
resources.n: The running example. Section 2.1: two passes keep about 75% of a standard model's token efficiency; a shared KV cache halves the cache but gains less; training looped from scratch beats upcycling.

resources.t: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
resources.n: Huginn, the design The Information compared Astra to. Its KV-cache sharing note is the source of the recurrent-depth argument the article does not cover.

resources.t: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
resources.n: Routed loop counts per token, 135M to 1.7B parameters, and a KV-sharing variant that reuses the first recursion's keys.

resources.t: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers
resources.n: Looping the middle half twice while matching per-token FLOPs, non-embedding parameters and KV cache: 6.8 to 18.0% of training FLOPs saved on the compute-optimal frontier, up to 54B.
Latent feedback from one token's top layer to the next token's input at 1B: shorter reasoning in the base model, an effect that disappears after instruction tuning.

resources.t: Beyond Parameters: Exploring Virtual Logic Depth for Scaling Laws
resources.n: Reusing weights leaves knowledge capacity nearly unchanged at fixed parameters but improves multi-step reasoning: the article's section 6.2.
